doc.title: Frank Wess interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: What made the Basie rhythm section
summary: Wess credits Basie's restrained piano style, complementing the band without overplaying.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: I’ll be darned. We’ve been trying to get different people’s different takes on what made the Basie rhythm section the Basie rhythm section. It’s like a term in jazz, you know? And what was that?
Basie did. Yeah, it was Basie’s rhythm section.

It was his style of playing, you know, that did it. He had a way of being effective, you know without being overpowering, you know, without playing too much. Most pianists would, with that type of band, they’d try to play too much when it’s really not necessary. Because you see you had the guitar keeping the rhythm already, you know, you don’t need it, so it’s up to you to complement what’s being played in the band and enhance it in a way, you know, that’s not what, you get a piano player, he wants to be a piano player. But you don’t need a piano player, you know what I mean? You need a musician that knows how to complement the band. So that’s what Basie was better than good at. He was the master of that.
